title: Material Movement
subtitle: Regenerative material recording device and artistic interactive installation

mainContent.content: A DEng installation repurposing a discarded CD player's laser head into a creative light-writing tool. Movement of matter becomes legible data and sensory scene at once.

content.title: Project poster showing the regenerative device, Arduino circuit diagram, and installation photos

mainContent.content: The poster communicates the full concept: recycling obsolete media through Arduino-driven laser modification to create a new material recording instrument.

content.title: Modified CD player mechanism with Arduino Uno circuit board and wiring diagram

mainContent.content: The transparent enclosure reveals the internal mechanics — Arduino Uno orchestrates motor speed, LED sequences, and sensor feedback for interactive light writing.

content.title: Overhead view: scratched CD spinning under laser, creating colorful diffracted light patterns

mainContent.content: The scratched CD surface diffracts laser light into colorful patterns, transforming material texture into visible visual data through motion and light.

From endpoint to cycle. Instead of discarding old hardware, the project asks what new material emerges when we re-read the familiar. The device slows observation down — visitors engage with the process of transformation.
